## Merged as `b127d40383620e88fb2ea4e5176e912bc9656dd0`; close blocked on an undeclared path

Gerrit 3190 reached `LLM-Review +1` (rebar review bot) and `Verified +1` (rebar CI bot) at 00:45
PDT on `db0fb9c44f92876295a4738c91a4cabd63655f31`, `submittable: true`, 0 unresolved. Submitted
revision-scoped via `scripts/gerrit_safe_submit.py 3190 --revision db0fb9c4...`; Gerrit rebased and
merged it as `b127d40383620e88fb2ea4e5176e912bc9656dd0`, carrying
`rebar-ticket: 7a7a-ceb9-e9a5-4d8e`.

`make verify` on the pushed tree: **rc=0, 20135 passed, 27 skipped, 1:28:46**
(`.rebar/scratch/verify-7a7a-v3/`).

### The close refused, and it was right

```
Error: cannot close: commit b127d40383620e88fb2ea4e5176e912bc9656dd0 changes
scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt, which the recorded file_impact does not declare,
so the work went beyond the reviewed plan.
```

The allowlist edit is this story's own work, not something the rebase introduced — it is present in
the pre-rebase commit `db0fb9c4` as well, and the commit message documents it:

> `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` loses the `_heldout` row and re-pins the surviving
> module to its measured post-merge count (6 + 30 = 36).

The **plan** also covers it, in two places: Approach step 2 is an entire bullet titled "Repoint the
vocabulary allowlist (measured, not hypothetical)", and AC2 requires
`python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` to exit 0 with that row removed and the survivor
re-pinned.

So the plan and the commit agreed; the `file_impact` array was the only place the path was missing —
it listed the 20 test modules and omitted the 21st file. The commit touches 21 files.

Worth recording as a general fact: **the close gate checks the committed file set against
`file_impact`, not against the description.** A path can be fully described in Approach and named in
an AC and still block the close if it is absent from the array.

### Remediation taken

`set_file_impact` now declares all 21 paths. Widening the array is a material plan change, so it
invalidates the plan-review attestation (`stale-material`); re-review started against the merged SHA
via `review_plan_start` (job `1793519435250714651-13593a6a612c40679719433ebccd06ee`). No `--force`
was used, and none is needed — this is the documented remediation path.
